name: tovel
author: time-agent
description: tovel v2. Clue 'L/S/x/k/n': L = days in the month (28-31), S = the column the 1st falls in (0 = Monday), x = a capital letter, k = 2..6, n = a date. The answer is that month's page: week rows of seven cells, the first row starting in column S, the dates 1..L in reading order, and EVERY date carrying a capital letter (token = the date immediately followed by its letter, e.g. '17B'). A weekday header line is allowed and ignored (any line containing no digit is skipped); whitespace and blank lines are free. RULE: score 1 iff the page is exactly right AND the dates d such that d and d+2 BOTH carry x and d falls on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday number exactly k AND the earliest of them is n - i.e. "x happens twice in the same school week with one day in between (Mon+Wed, Tue+Thu, Wed+Fri) exactly k times, and the first time is on the nth". WHY v2 (the v1 leak): in run lad-tovel-v1-1 neither player found the rule and both scored by farming. v1's accepted pages depended only on (days, start, k) and were invariant under renaming letters, so tovel1b harvested one accepted page per (days,start,k) triple - 108 of the 140 triples - replayed it with the letters renamed and reached 83 % with no theory at all ("a letter pattern that scores 1 keeps scoring 1 when the identity of every letter is renamed, so only the shape counts... replaying a winning shape under a different clue LETTER scored 173/173"); tovel1a tuned a random lettering density per k (~0.65) and got 48 % blind, because "count == k" alone is hit by a tuned random page about one time in six. FIX (idea (b) of the refiner brief, in its strongest form): the clue names a date, and that date must be the FIRST counted day. This (1) pins the page to the clue rather than to the triple, so a harvested page transfers only when its own first counted day happens to equal the new clue's n; (2) multiplies the harvestable clue classes from 140 to 1229 (mean 8.8 first-days per triple), which cannot be farmed in six 0.5 s rounds; (3) drops the tuned-random-page rate from 16.8 % to 1.5 %, because the count and the anchor must both come out right; and (4) is the softening the class also needed - the clue now points at a day where the thing happens, so a player can read the relation off the demos ("day n and day n+2 are always x") instead of having to guess distance 2, and every demo carries a two-apart pair EARLIER than n that does not count, which shows the weekend/week-break exclusion positively. Also acted on the judge's advice: solve() now requires, in every demo, a weekend-reaching pair (Thu/Fri start) and a week-break-crossing pair (Sat/Sun start) within three days of a counted pair (100 % of demos), plus a non-counting pair before day n (92 %). INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH (private): (1) one demo shows a calendar page and 'L/S' is its shape - the first row holds 7-S dates; that format gate is kid-easy but nothing scores until it is right. (2) x names the letter being counted; the other letters are noise. (3) n is a date, and in every demo day n carries x and so does day n+2 - the relation. (4) k counts them; which pairs count? solve() guarantees that in EVERY demo each rival count differs from k (x next door, a week apart, two apart anywhere, two apart inside a week row, three apart, the number of x's, the same relation for any letter, cells-not-pairs, and the no-x-in-between variant). (5) the last step is the weekend: a pair reaching into Sat/Sun, or stepping over the week break, does not count - now visible because such a pair sits before the clue's own "first" day. A player who gets everything but the weekend lands at 28 % (a real partial tier); one who repeats the pair weekly from day n (never leaving n's weekday, so the weekend rule is never needed) lands at 32 % overall - 77 % at k=2, 0 % at k=6, where the month is too short to repeat. WITNESSES (600 fresh clues each): empty, spaces, newlines, '0', '1', 'x', '1'*100, a 4000-char junk string, the clue itself, a bare date grid with no letters, an all-x page, a one-letter page - all 0.00 %; the best constant answer 1.00 %; a tuned random lettering 0.5-1.5 % at every density tried (v1: 2.7-16.8 %). Wrong-relation constructors on a correct page honouring the clue's first day: next door 0.00 %, three apart 1.35 %, a week apart 5.22 %, two apart anywhere 15.00 %, two apart inside a week row 27.67 %, the true rule 100 %. THE HARVEST ATTACK (the v1 leak, measured directly): take a demo answer for clue A, rename every letter (A's marked letter -> B's), submit for clue B with the same (days,start,k) - v1 100.00 %, v2 11.50 % (678 transfers). Matching (days,start,k,n) too still transfers at 100 %, but that is 1229 classes and blind probing lands on one about 1.5 % of the time, so the ceiling on pure farming is ~12 %. A player who additionally realises the page may be slid up or down by whole weeks to move the anchor gets 61 % on the week-aligned third of clues - that transform requires reading the calendar's week periodicity, i.e. most of the rule, so it is left open as a near-crack tier. Shape attacks on a page with the correct count: one row, one token per line, zero-padded dates, an extra day, a dropped day, lower case, '17 B' instead of '17B' - all 0.00 %; header/no header, tabs and blank lines 100 % (robust about form, strict about content); a page laid out from column 0 scores 11 % = exactly the S=0 clues. The scorer never raises and never returns a non-binary value on 20000 random junk strings (worst 0.05 ms), agrees with an independent re-implementation of the stated rule on 9000 well-formed mutated answers with 0 disagreements, and is 419 chars. solve() scores 1 on 6000/6000 seeds, 22 ms average / 220 ms worst, and randomises the header style, the alphabet (4-5 letters), the chain structure and the decoy placement, so no two demos look alike. Human-designed for the 'everyday time and place' direction: the object is a family calendar, the measurement has no name, and recognising the calendar is necessary but nowhere near sufficient.

def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    L = r.choice([28, 29, 30, 31, 30, 31])
    S = r.randrange(7)
    x = r.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
    k = r.randint(2, 6)
    E = [d for d in range(1, L - 1) if (d - 1 + S) % 7 < 3]
    E = E[:max(1, len(E) - k + 1)]
    if len(E) > 1 and r.random() < 0.8:
        E = E[1:]
    return "%d/%d/%s/%d/%d" % (L, S, x, k, r.choice(E))
solve:
def cnts(g, S, x):
    L = len(g)
    C = [i for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x and (i + S) % 7 < 3]
    D = [i for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x and (i + S) % 7 > 2]
    h1 = sum(1 for i in range(L - 1) if g[i] == g[i + 1] == x)  # next door
    h2 = sum(1 for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x)
    h3 = sum(1 for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x and (i + S) % 7 < 5)
    h4 = sum(1 for i in range(L - 7) if g[i] == g[i + 7] == x)  # a week apart
    h5 = g.count(x)                                
    h6 = sum(1 for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] and (i + S) % 7 < 3)  # any letter, two apart
    h7 = sum(1 for i in range(L - 3) if g[i] == g[i + 3] == x)
    h8 = sum(1 for i in range(L - 1) if g[i] == g[i + 1] == x and (i + S) % 7 < 4)
    h10 = sum(1 for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x and g[i + 1] != x and (i + S) % 7 < 3)
    cells = set()
    for i in C:
        cells |= {i, i + 2}
    return C, (h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8, len(cells), h10), D
def render(g, S, r):
    head = r.choice(["Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su", "MON TUE WED THU FRI SAT SUN", "M T W T F S S"]).split()
    cells = [""] * S + ["%d%s" % (i + 1, g[i]) for i in range(len(g))]
    while len(cells) % 7:
        cells.append("")
    out = [" ".join(w.rjust(3) for w in head).rstrip()]
    for j in range(0, len(cells), 7):
        out.append(" ".join(c.rjust(3) for c in cells[j:j + 7]).rstrip())
    return "\n".join(out)
def chk(clue, s):
    a = clue.split("/"); L = int(a[0]); S = int(a[1])
    R = [l.split() for l in s.split("\n") if any(h.isdigit() for h in l)]
    T = [t for r in R for t in r]
    return int(len(T) == L > 0 and all(t[:-1] == str(i + 1) and t[-1] > "9" for i, t in enumerate(T))
               and len(R[0]) == 7 - S and all(len(r) == 7 for r in R[1:-1]) and 0 < len(R[-1]) < 8
               and len(C := [i for i in range(L - 2) if T[i][-1] == T[i + 2][-1] == a[2] and (i + S) % 7 < 3]) == int(a[3])
               and C[0] == int(a[4]) - 1)
def solve(clue):
    a = clue.split("/"); L = int(a[0]); S = int(a[1]); x = a[2]; k = int(a[3]); f = int(a[4]) - 1
    r = random.Random(clue)
    pool = [c for c in string.ascii_uppercase if c != x]
    slots = [i for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 < 3 and i > f]
    for att in range(1200):
        want_early = att < 500
        want_near = att < 700
        others = r.sample(pool, r.randint(3, 4))
        g = [r.choice(others) for _ in range(L)]
        chosen = [f]
        while len(chosen) < k:  # chains keep x sparse
            near = [i for i in slots if i not in chosen and any(abs(i - j) == 2 for j in chosen)]
            chosen.append(r.choice(near) if near and r.random() < 0.75 else
                          r.choice([i for i in slots if i not in chosen]))
        for i in chosen:
            g[i] = x; g[i + 2] = x
        moves = []                  # decoys
        for want in ((3, 4), (5, 6)):
            cand = [(i, i + 2) for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 in want]
            r.shuffle(cand)
            cand.sort(key=lambda p: (not (want_early and p[0] < f),
                                     min(abs(p[0] - c) for c in chosen) > 3))
            moves.append(cand)
        moves.append([(i, i + 1) for i in range(L - 1)])
        moves.append([(i, i + 7) for i in range(L - 7)])
        moves.append([(i + 1, i + 1) for i in chosen])
        for cand in moves:
            if cand is moves[2] or cand is moves[3]:
                r.shuffle(cand)
            for i, j in cand:
                sv = (g[i], g[j]); g[i] = x; g[j] = x
                C = cnts(g, S, x)[0]
                if len(C) == k and C[0] == f:
                    break
                g[i], g[j] = sv
        free = [i for i in slots if x not in (g[i], g[i + 2])]
        r.shuffle(free)
        for i in free[:2]:  # other letter, two apart
            c = r.choice(others); g[i] = c; g[i + 2] = c
        C, H, D = cnts(g, S, x)
        if len(C) != k or C[0] != f or any(h == k for h in H):
            continue
        p1 = [i for i in D if (i + S) % 7 in (3, 4)]  # reaches the weekend
        p2 = [i for i in D if (i + S) % 7 in (5, 6)]  # steps over the week break
        if not p1 or not p2:
            continue
        if want_near and (min(abs(i - c) for i in p1 for c in C) > 3 or min(abs(i - c) for i in p2 for c in C) > 3):
            continue  # decoys beside a counted pair
        if want_early and f > 0 and not [i for i in D if i < f]:
            continue  # ... and one before day n
        if len(set(g)) < 4 or (att < 900 and g.count(x) > (0.28 + 0.035 * k) * L):
            continue
        s = render(g, S, r)
        if chk(clue, s):
            return s
    return ""
